Convert a query result to a quanteda corpus

Source: R/outputs-corpus.R
as_corpus.Rd

Hands a speech result to quanteda as a corpus: one document per row, named by docid_field, with text from text_field and every other column as a document variable (docvar). Docvars keep their names, values and types: dates stay Dates and flags stay logical.

Usage

as_corpus(x, text_field = "content", docid_field = "action_id")

Arguments

x

A tibble or data frame, or a lazy table from an ausparl function with collect = FALSE, with one row per document.

text_field

Name of the character column holding the text. Results fetched with include_text = FALSE have no content column; fetch them with include_text = TRUE.

docid_field

Name of the column holding the document names. Its values must be unique and not NA.

Value

A quanteda corpus with one document per row of x.

Details

x is usually the output of get_speeches() or search_speeches_by_terms(), possibly after add_*() helpers such as add_party(); the added columns become docvars.

A lazy table (collect = FALSE) is collected first. A result with a content column is held to the text size ceiling, getOption("ausparl.max_rows_text"); above it the call is an error.

The text is never edited. NA text is passed to quanteda as it is, and quanteda's own conversion applies (it currently becomes an empty document, with a warning).

This function only builds the corpus; tokenising, document-feature matrices and analysis are left to quanteda.

See also

get_speeches(), search_speeches_by_terms()

Examples

db_connect(sample = TRUE)
speeches <- get_speeches(from = 2002, to = 2002, limit = 20)
corp <- as_corpus(speeches)
corp
